en: Now, obviously, when you are working on a
real project, you probably don't wanna
encode HTML code like this.
Instead, you might want separate files. You
might want pages
where you have your index.html file for the
main page, your courses.html file for the
courses page, and your 404.html file for,
well, the 404 errors.
And then maybe you also want some assets
here like your style.css file and maybe some
frontend script. So therefore, I did now use
AI to generate some dummy content and styles
here. So in all these HTML files
and in the CSS file, I got some styles and
some dummy content. And you find these files
attached so that you can use them if you
wanna follow along.
index.ts has now also been changed slightly.
In there, I'm now importing these styles
HTML files. So the 3 HTML files I added
here, I'm importing them because Bun
natively supports HTML imports. That's not a
standard JavaScript or TypeScript feature,
but it's a Bun feature. Now, what's the
purpose of adding those imports? Well, I'm
in the end passing those imported
objects, which these things here turn out to
be,
to a servePage helper function, which I
added, this function here. It's a very
simple helper function. It's just there to
construct the response. So that I don't have
to repeat that new response code over and
over again.
And in there I get that page thing which is
of type BunHtmlBundle. That's what these
imported things are. And in there we have a
couple of properties, specifically a files
and an index property. And the index
property simply is a path to that file, to
the HTML file.
So if I would move that around, the import
path would update and page index, this code
would stay the same. That's the advantage of
using this approach.
We're then using bun.file here, which is
another native Bun API for reading a file,
to read the file content of that HTML file.
And then I set the
appropriate header. So that's how I'm
returning these HTML files as responses.
Now, there also is one other new route I
added here, which is simply there to handle
requests to
/assets/styles.css because in those pages, I
make that request or The browser will make
that request because I'm linking the
stylesheet here.
And that's simply needed to make sure that
the styles are served correctly.
And with that out of the way, if I reload,
that's what the page looks like right now.
And for invalid paths, I got a proper 404
page too.
And that's of course therefore another
convenient feature, but we can still do
better when it comes to setting up a web
server and using Bun for making our life
easier.
